To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of prognostics scores can improve survival in HCV infected patients after RT and that the use of these scores can identify patients with a high risk to die after RT.
retransplantation in patients infected with hepatitis C virus is a good option for survival but it is associated with a high rate of morbidity and mortality.
retransplantation in patients who develop severe forms of HCV recurrence after primary transplantation is associated with a poor outcome.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of prognosticators for RT selection and the early treatment of severe hepatitis C recurrent disease are the best strategies to improve the results after RT in HCV-inflicted patients.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RT is a reasonable option for patients with severe hepatitis recurrence and fibrosis progression.
the use of prognostics scores in HCV-inflicted patients after RT is useful to identify those with a high risk to die.
RT in patients with HCV recurrence after LT should be performed only in patients with a low risk of mortality and with a good quality of life.
The main takeaway from our work is that
patients with severe hepatitis recurrence after LT are at high risk of death and RT should not be offered to them.
patients who undergo retransplantation for hepatitis C virus recurrence are a very heterogeneous group of patients.
the use of prognostics scores in HCV-inflicted patients with cirrhosis undergoing RT can help to identify patients with a high risk mortality, and thus avoid unnecessary RT.
